source_note: All values come from WebSearch results (40 searches: 24 for market data and FX, 16 for fiscal terms). WebFetch and the container network are blocked, so no page was opened. 'quote' is the text exactly as the search result gave it: sometimes page text, often the search tool's own summary wording; none was checked against the page. 'url' is the page the result cites; url_certain=false where the result did not tie the statement to one listed page. Nothing was filled from memory.

conventions.v: Only a number a search result states for that exact item; null otherwise.
conventions.derived_v: Arithmetic on stated numbers, shown in 'working' (e.g. price x shares). No result states it; use with care.
conventions.alternatives: Other stated values for the same item (different date or basis).
conventions.confidence: high = dated within a few days of 26 Nov 2026; medium = dated Oct-Nov 2026 or a Nov 2026 document without a price date; low = undated, stale or conflicting.
conventions.units: share_price per share in the listed currency; shares_M in millions; market_cap_M, cash_M and debt_M in millions of the stated currency; ownership_pct in %.
conventions.fiscal: rate_pct holds a single stated rate; sliding or tiered regimes use rate_min_pct/rate_max_pct, tiers or components with rate_pct null. confirmed = true (a result states the rate for this item), 'partial' (structure or band stated, details missing) or false.

corporate_tax_pct.quote: A BC CCPC pays 11% on its first $500,000 of active business income and 27% above that. BC's provincial general rate is 12%, and its 2026 provincial rates are 2% on income eligible for the small business deduction and 12% on other income.
corporate_tax_pct.note: 27% is the general combined rate (15% federal + 12% BC).

gold_royalty.base: three state levies: Net Proceeds of Minerals Tax on net proceeds (2-5% sliding), Gold and Silver Excise Tax on Nevada gross revenue (0.75%/1.10%), and Commerce Tax on Nevada gross revenue (0.051%)

components.name: Net Proceeds of Minerals Tax
components.base: net proceeds (gross revenue less allowable mining, processing and transport deductions); the rate depends on the ratio of net proceeds to gross proceeds; royalties are taxed at 5%
components.quote: The tax rate for royalties is 5%. The tax rate applied to the net proceeds is based on a sliding scale between 2% and 5%, depending on the ratio of net proceeds to gross proceeds.

components.name: Gold and Silver Excise Tax (NRS 363D)
components.base: Nevada gross revenue; applies only above US$20M a year
components.quote: This applies to Nevada gross revenue above $20 million a year, at 0.75% on revenue from $20 million to $150 million and 1.10% on revenue above $150 million (NRS 363D.010, per the statute's rate schedule).

components.name: Commerce Tax (mining category)
components.quote: The statute sets the mining category at 0.051 percent of Nevada gross revenue above $4,000,000.

gold_royalty.notes: Mining companies also pay the Modified Business Tax on payroll; the rate conflicts across sources (1.554%, 1.853% or about 1.378%).
gold_royalty.quote: The tax rate for royalties is 5%. The tax rate applied to the net proceeds is based on a sliding scale between 2% and 5%, depending on the ratio of net proceeds to gross proceeds.

copper_royalty.base: Net Proceeds of Minerals Tax on net proceeds (2-5% sliding) plus Commerce Tax (0.051% of Nevada gross revenue above US$4M); the Gold and Silver Excise Tax does not apply to copper revenue

components.name: Net Proceeds of Minerals Tax
components.base: net proceeds; the rate depends on the ratio of net proceeds to gross proceeds
components.quote: The tax rate for royalties is 5%. The tax rate applied to the net proceeds is based on a sliding scale between 2% and 5%, depending on the ratio of net proceeds to gross proceeds.

components.name: Commerce Tax (mining category)
components.quote: The statute sets the mining category at 0.051 percent of Nevada gross revenue above $4,000,000.

copper_royalty.notes: The NPOM result is not commodity-specific; it applies to 'the gross revenue from the minerals extracted minus allowable deductions'. NRS 363D is titled 'TAX ON GROSS REVENUE OF GOLD AND SILVER MINING BUSINESSES'.
copper_royalty.quote: The tax rate for royalties is 5%. The tax rate applied to the net proceeds is based on a sliding scale between 2% and 5%, depending on the ratio of net proceeds to gross proceeds.

corporate_tax_pct.quote: One notes that a C corporation pays no state income tax, so its combined rate is just the 21% federal rate.
corporate_tax_pct.note: Federal 21%, plus no Nevada corporate income tax ('Sources agree the state levies neither a corporate nor a personal income tax.'). Secondary sources.

gold_royalty.base: Mining royalty (Law 21.591, from 1 Jan 2024), banded by annual sales in metric tonnes of fine copper equivalent (MTFC) and charged on adjusted mining operating income (RIOMA); not gold-specific

tiers.note: Exempt per an older (2019) Lexology summary that predates Law 21.591.
tiers.quote: An older Lexology summary gives a progressive rate of between 0.5 per cent and 4.5 per cent for the 12,000–50,000 band, and says companies at or below 12,000 tonnes are exempt.

tiers.note: Marginal rates by production level (EY, on the approved law); Lexology (2019) gave 0.5%-4.5%.
tiers.quote: the marginal tax rates fluctuate from 0.4% to 4.4% depending on the levels of production for sales above the equivalent of 12,000 but below 50,000 MTFC, and progressive tax rates ranging from 5% to 14% above 50,000 MTFC.

tiers.band: over 50,000 MTFC, copper half or less of sales
tiers.note: Reported by a commercial web page; EY gives 5% to 14% above 50,000 MTFC. The sources conflict.
tiers.quote: Operators with half or less of their sales from copper follow a different scale, reported as 5% up to 34.5%

gold_royalty.notes: The result says 'Nothing in these results sets a gold-specific rate.' How gold sales convert to copper equivalent was not confirmed.
gold_royalty.quote: the marginal tax rates fluctuate from 0.4% to 4.4% depending on the levels of production for sales above the equivalent of 12,000 but below 50,000 MTFC, and progressive tax rates ranging from 5% to 14% above 50,000 MTFC.

copper_royalty.base: For operators selling more than 50,000 MTFC with over half of revenue from copper: 1% ad valorem on copper sales plus a margin component of 8-26% on RIOMA (rate set by mining operating margin = RIOMA / mining operating income x 100), with a cap on the total burden. Mid-size producers (12,000-50,000 MTFC) pay the 0.4-4.4% marginal scale in gold_royalty.tiers.

components.name: ad valorem component
components.base: copper sales (operators above 50,000 MTFC); reduced or offset when RIOMA is negative
components.quote: Sources agree on a flat 1% charge on copper sales for operators above the equivalent of 50,000 metric tons of fine copper.

components.name: margin component
components.quote: One summary describes the schedule as 8% at a margin of 20 or less, rising to 12% at a margin of 45, reaching 26% at a margin of 60, and staying at 26% above that
components.note: Commercial web page; check the bands against the statute.

components.name: cap on total tax burden
components.cap_pct: 45.5 (up to 80,000 t) / 46.5 (above 80,000 t) of adjusted mining taxable income
components.quote: One says total tax is capped at 46.5% of adjusted mining taxable income. The same source gives 45.5% for operators up to 80,000 tonnes

copper_royalty.notes: Structure confirmed by EY; the margin bands come from a commercial page. 'The law took effect on 1 January 2024.'
copper_royalty.quote: Sources agree on a flat 1% charge on copper sales for operators above the equivalent of 50,000 metric tons of fine copper.

corporate_tax_pct.quote: Law 21.850 reduces the first-category rate from 27% to 23% by 2029 and creates a tax stability regime for investments starting at US$50mn.
corporate_tax_pct.note: First Category tax. A Rio Times piece (Apr 2026) called the cut a proposal ('First Category corporate income tax cuts from 27% to 23% gradually'). Neither enactment nor the rate that applies in 2026-27 was confirmed. Dividend withholding not covered.

gold_royalty.base: Mining royalty on quarterly operating profit (minimum 1% of sales); plus Special Mining Tax of 2-8.4% on operating profit; GEM of 4-13.12% only under tax stability agreements
gold_royalty.type: national mining royalty plus special mining tax

components.name: Mining royalty (Regalia Minera)
components.base: quarterly operating profit; minimum 1% of sales
components.quote: PwC lists it at 1% - 12% (minimum 1% of sales). It is calculated quarterly.

components.name: Special Mining Tax (SMT / IEM)
components.base: operating profit from sales of metallic minerals
components.quote: PwC gives 2% - 8.4%. It applies only to operating profit.

components.name: Special Mining Contribution (GEM)
components.base: applies only to companies with valid tax stability agreements
components.quote: PwC gives 4% - 13.12%. Lexology notes that the GEM is only applicable to the mining companies that have valid tax stability agreements.

gold_royalty.notes: The sources are dated (PwC 2020). Lexology on the royalty base: 'the basis is the operating profit or the sales revenue of the quarter (in the case of the mining royalty)'. Not commodity-specific.
gold_royalty.quote: PwC lists it at 1% - 12% (minimum 1% of sales). It is calculated quarterly.

copper_royalty.base: Mining royalty on quarterly operating profit (minimum 1% of sales); plus Special Mining Tax of 2-8.4% on operating profit; GEM of 4-13.12% only under tax stability agreements
copper_royalty.type: national mining royalty plus special mining tax
copper_royalty.notes: Same regime as gold (see gold_royalty.components). The sources are dated (PwC 2020).
copper_royalty.quote: PwC lists it at 1% - 12% (minimum 1% of sales). It is calculated quarterly.

corporate_tax_pct.quote: The general income tax rate is 29.5 percent.
corporate_tax_pct.note: 'Projects with a stability agreement pay a higher rate. Per the IMF, the rate is two percentage points higher than the rate in effect at the time of signing.' Dividend withholding not covered.
